title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly used Flock license plate cameras to search one plate 41 times and another plate 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. The lieutenant admitted the lookups were not for official law enforcement work. A resident had filed a complaint alleging the lieutenant was stalking them and that they feared for their family's safety. The lieutenant claimed the drivers were lurking near the lieutenant's home and described a contentious familial relationship with one vehicle owner. An internal affairs investigation found the lieutenant violated department rules and suspended the lieutenant for two days. The lieutenant is not facing criminal charges and is not being named.

Flock cameras have drawn privacy and security concerns, including recent opposition in Harris County and vandalism in Houston. A University of Houston law professor said improper access alone is usually an administrative or ethical violation, and escalation would require clear intent to harm. The lieutenant said the information was not shared or used. ABC13 has contacted the lieutenant and the sheriff's office and is awaiting a response.
